title: Cola-colored urine
objective: Recognize rhabdomyolysis from muscle pain, dark urine and a high CK, and give early IV fluid while watching potassium and kidney function

brief.situation: 08:20 on a progressive care unit. Mr. Hale, 67, was admitted overnight after being found on his kitchen floor, where he had lain for about a day after a fall. His thighs ache and the urine in his catheter bag is dark brown.
handover: CK on admission 38,000; potassium 5.4; creatinine above his baseline. On telemetry.

Orders: the ordered isotonic IV fluid at the high rate to keep urine output at or above the target in the order, hourly urine, potassium and creatinine every 4 hours, and the provider called for urine below the target, a potassium rising or any ECG change.
His home list includes a potassium supplement and an ACE inhibitor, both due at 09:00. The provider is on the unit.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Assess and act as you think the patient needs. Each assessment takes the time on its button.
Partway through you are asked to write what you think is happening. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: Mr. Hale's urine is falling and his T waves are peaked. What is happening, and what do you do?

parts.label: What is happening
parts.criteria: A long lie, muscle pain, dark urine and a CK of 38,000 are rhabdomyolysis; falling urine and peaked T waves mean kidney injury and rising potassium.
parts.modelAnswer: He has rhabdomyolysis from the long lie: sore muscles, dark urine, a huge CK. Now the urine is falling and the T waves are peaked, so his kidneys are failing and his potassium is climbing.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Keep the high-rate fluid; hold the potassium supplement and ACE inhibitor; provider now for the potassium and nephrology; keep him on telemetry; hand off.
parts.modelAnswer: Keep the fluid going, hold the potassium and the ACE inhibitor, call the provider now for the potassium and nephrology, keep him on telemetry, and hand off.

scoring.modelReasoning: A day on the floor, aching thighs, dark urine and a CK of 38,000 are rhabdomyolysis. Early high-rate isotonic fluid protects the kidneys, with hourly urine, and the potassium supplement and ACE inhibitor are held. When the urine falls below target and the T waves peak, the kidneys are failing and potassium is rising: the provider comes now.
